With a lower feedstock brown grease price of $0.47/kg, the MFSP of the HC via the HEFA-SPK pathway is estimated at approximately $4.3/gge for feedstock collected from 50 miles (Table 14) and $3.8/gge for feedstocks from a 100-mile collection radius. The conversion cost without considering feedstock cost would be $2.4/gge and $1.9/gge, respectively. This means that HC’s minimum selling prices are still higher than that of the conventional jet fuel with brown grease, but the delta between the two is improved. Hydrolysis breaks down insoluble organic matter into simple monomers via hydrolytic microorganisms. Proteins are converted to amino acids, lipids into fatty acids, starch to glucose, and carbohydrates to monomeric sugars. 2. Acidogenesis converts simple sugars and acids to volatile fatty acids and alcohols via acidogens. This is the fastest step in the AD process, which involves complex consortia of bacteria, including bacteriocides, Clostridia, Bifidobacteria, Streptococci, and Enterobacteriaceae (Weiland 2010). 3. Acetogenesis further converts volatile fatty acids to acetate, CO , and H . 2 2 4. Methanogenesis converts acetate and H to methane (CH ) and CO via methanogenic 2 4 2 bacteria. 23 This report is available at no cost from the National Laboratory of the Rockies (NLR) at www.nlr.gov/publications. The consortium of microbial populations needs to be maintained to stabilize the AD process and increase biogas production efficiency. Figure 16. Steps in the AD process. Source: Bhatt and Tao (2020) The AD technology facilitates organic decomposition and reduces inorganic matter in the absence of oxygen (Global Methane Initiative 2016). These organic materials are converted to final products, which are mainly biogas, digestate (liquid form in most cases), and a combination of solid and liquid effluents derived from digestate treatments (Chen and Nebling 2014).
